statement: Every 3-connected claw-free graph has a Hamiltonian cycle.
definitions: Claw-free: no induced subgraph isomorphic to K_{1,3}. 3-connected: at least 4 vertices and the graph stays connected after deleting any set of at most 2 vertices. Graph finite simple undirected.
ground_truth_witness: The triangle-replaced (inflated) Petersen graph on V={0,...,29} with 45 edges, E=[[0,1],[0,2],[0,3],[1,2],[1,12],[2,15],[3,4],[3,5],[4,5],[4,6],[5,18],[6,7],[6,8],[7,8],[7,9],[8,21],[9,10],[9,11],[10,11],[10,13],[11,24],[12,13],[12,14],[13,14],[14,27],[15,16],[15,17],[16,17],[16,22],[17,25],[18,19],[18,20],[19,20],[19,26],[20,28],[21,22],[21,23],[22,23],[23,29],[24,25],[24,26],[25,26],[27,28],[27,29],[28,29]]. It is obtained from the Petersen graph by replacing each vertex with a triangle and attaching the three original edges to the three corners. It is 3-regular, 3-connected and claw-free (every vertex lies in a triangle, so no induced K_{1,3}), but an exhaustive search shows it has no Hamiltonian cycle. The Matthews-Sumner conjecture therefore cannot be weakened from 4-connected to 3-connected.

skeptic.objection: Precise and false. Verified on the given 30-vertex edge list: cubic, connected, 3-connected (no 1- or 2-vertex cut), claw-free (no induced K_{1,3}), exactly 10 triangles whose contraction is isomorphic to the Petersen graph, and no Hamiltonian cycle (backtracking search). Distinct object and distinct claim from the roster's Petersen items (cb-mse-r05/cb-gt15 are '3-connected cubic => Hamiltonian'); a solver must know or build the triangle-inflation and argue that a Hamiltonian cycle in the inflation would project to one in Petersen - a genuine argument. Only caveat: it is Petersen-derived, so the roster's Petersen density grows further.
